idiom_name: `XxxMother` test class with static factory methods
implementation_notes: Java ships nothing for test data, so the mother is a package-private test-source class with static factory methods that return fully initialised domain objects, exactly as in the java-design-patterns reference example. JUnit Jupiter's @BeforeEach/@BeforeAll cover per-class fixtures and @ParameterizedTest covers input variation, but cross-class canned examples remain hand-written; records with compact constructors (Java 16+) remove most construction noise, so reserve the mother for multi-object aggregates and named business states. Keep it in src/test/java so it never reaches the production artifact.
pitfalls: Static mutable fields in the mother are shared across the entire test JVM and race under JUnit 5 parallel execution.
Returning a cached instance instead of constructing a new one lets one test's mutation change another test's fixture.
Mothers that use reflection or the no-arg constructor to bypass validation produce objects that cannot exist in production and hide real bugs.

Package-private static methods in the same package as production code compile into the test classpath only, but an accidental import from main code still breaks the build - keep the mother's package test-only and its visibility minimal.
